measure: a change or difference between two periods
gold_sql:
WITH restricted_measurements AS (
    SELECT
        apm.measurement_id,
        apm.allele_id,
        apm.measurement_value,
        apm.experiment_date,
        apm.measurement_source_id
    FROM allele_peptide_measurements apm
    WHERE apm.measurement_value IS NOT NULL
      AND apm.experiment_date IS NOT NULL
      AND apm.measurement_source_id IS NOT NULL
      AND apm.measurement_value > (
          SELECT AVG(apm2.measurement_value)
          FROM allele_peptide_measurements apm2
          WHERE apm2.allele_id = apm.allele_id
            AND apm2.measurement_value IS NOT NULL
      )
),
ranked_by_allele AS (
    SELECT
        rm.measurement_id,
        rm.allele_id,
        rm.measurement_value,
        rm.experiment_date,
        rm.measurement_source_id,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY rm.allele_id
            ORDER BY rm.experiment_date
        ) AS date_rank
    FROM restricted_measurements rm
),
survivors AS (
    SELECT
        rba.allele_id,
        rba.measurement_value,
        rba.experiment_date,
        ms.source_year,
        a.allele_name
    FROM ranked_by_allele rba
    JOIN alleles a
      ON a.allele_id = rba.allele_id
    JOIN measurement_sources ms
      ON ms.source_id = rba.measurement_source_id
    WHERE rba.date_rank = 1
),
period_aggregates AS (
    SELECT
        allele_id,
        allele_name,
        MIN(source_year) AS first_source_year,
        MAX(source_year) AS last_source_year,
        COUNT(*) AS survivor_count,
        AVG(measurement_value) AS avg_measurement_value
    FROM survivors
    GROUP BY allele_id, allele_name
)
SELECT
    allele_id AS allele_id,
    allele_name AS allele_name,
    first_source_year AS first_source_year,
    last_source_year AS last_source_year,
    survivor_count AS survivor_count,
    avg_measurement_value AS avg_measurement_value,
    (last_source_year - first_source_year) AS source_year_change
FROM period_aggregates
ORDER BY source_year_change DESC, survivor_count DESC, allele_name ASC
question: For each HLA allele, consider only measurements with a non-null measurement value, experiment date, and measurement source, and keep only those measurements whose value is greater than that allele’s own average measurement value. For the earliest such measurement date per allele, report the allele ID, allele name, the earliest source year, the latest source year, the number of surviving measurements, the average measurement value across those surviving measurements, and the change in source year from earliest to latest, ordered by the source-year change from largest to smallest, then by survivor count, then by allele name.

columns: average measurement value across surviving measurements

measure: a maximum or minimum, with the row that attains it
gold_sql:
WITH version_stats AS (
  SELECT
    dv.output_id,
    COUNT(*) AS version_count,
    MIN(dv.version_date) AS first_version_date,
    MAX(dv.version_date) AS last_version_date
  FROM data_versions dv
  WHERE dv.version_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY dv.output_id
),
typed_outputs AS (
  SELECT
    do.output_id,
    do.output_name,
    ot.type_name
  FROM digital_outputs do
  JOIN output_types ot
    ON do.output_type = ot.type_id
),
eligible_outputs AS (
  SELECT
    t.output_id,
    t.output_name,
    t.type_name,
    vs.version_count,
    vs.first_version_date,
    vs.last_version_date,
    (julianday(vs.last_version_date) - julianday(vs.first_version_date)) AS version_span_days
  FROM typed_outputs t
  JOIN version_stats vs
    ON t.output_id = vs.output_id
  WHERE t.type_name IS NOT NULL
    AND vs.version_count >= 2
),
max_span_output AS (
  SELECT eo.*
  FROM eligible_outputs eo
  ORDER BY eo.version_span_days DESC, eo.version_count DESC, eo.output_id ASC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT
  output_id,
  output_name,
  type_name,
  version_count,
  first_version_date,
  last_version_date,
  version_span_days
FROM max_span_output
question: Which single digital output has the longest span in days between its first recorded version date and its last recorded version date, considering only outputs that have at least two recorded versions? For that output, report its ID, name, type name, total number of versions, first version date, last version date, and the version span in days.

gate.row_grain: A single digital output with its version span metrics and type information
gate.why: The question specifies selecting a single digital output based on the longest version span among those with at least two versions, and explicitly names all seven attributes to be reported.

measure: a maximum or minimum, with the row that attains it
gold_sql:
WITH article_oa AS (
  SELECT
    a.article_id,
    a.title AS article_title,
    j.journal_id,
    j.title AS journal_title,
    j.gold_oa_apc,
    g.apc AS term_apc,
    g.content_licence,
    g.alternative_licence,
    COUNT(g.term_id) OVER (PARTITION BY j.journal_id) AS term_count,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY j.journal_id
      ORDER BY CAST(COALESCE(g.apc, j.gold_oa_apc, '0') AS REAL) DESC, a.article_id
    ) AS apc_rank
  FROM articles AS a
  JOIN journals AS j
    ON a.journal_id = j.journal_id
  LEFT JOIN gold_oa_terms AS g
    ON g.journal_id = j.journal_id
),
journal_stats AS (
  SELECT
    journal_id,
    journal_title,
    COUNT(DISTINCT article_id) AS article_count,
    AVG(CAST(COALESCE(term_apc, gold_oa_apc, '0') AS REAL)) AS avg_apc,
    MAX(CAST(COALESCE(term_apc, gold_oa_apc, '0') AS REAL)) AS max_apc,
    MIN(CAST(COALESCE(term_apc, gold_oa_apc, '0') AS REAL)) AS min_apc
  FROM article_oa
  GROUP BY journal_id, journal_title
)
SELECT
  journal_id,
  journal_title,
  article_count,
  ROUND(avg_apc, 2) AS avg_apc,
  max_apc AS headline_max_apc,
  min_apc AS min_apc,
  ROUND(CAST(article_count AS REAL) / NULLIF((SELECT SUM(article_count) FROM journal_stats), 0), 4) AS article_share,
  CASE
    WHEN max_apc = (SELECT MAX(max_apc) FROM journal_stats) THEN 'highest_apc_journal'
    ELSE 'other_journal'
  END AS apc_label
FROM journal_stats
ORDER BY headline_max_apc DESC, journal_title
question: For each journal, can you report the journal identifier and journal title, the number of articles published in that journal, the average article-processing charge across that journal’s gold open-access terms and journal-level gold APC value, the highest such APC seen for that journal, the lowest such APC seen for that journal, and that journal’s share of all articles in the dataset? Also label each journal as the one with the highest maximum APC overall or as another journal, and order the results by the highest APC in descending order and then by journal title.

naive_sql:
SELECT
  p.paper_id,
  p.title,
  COUNT(coi.conflict_id) AS max_conflict_count
FROM papers AS p
JOIN conflicts_of_interest AS coi
  ON coi.paper_id = p.paper_id
GROUP BY p.paper_id, p.title
HAVING COUNT(coi.conflict_id) = (
  SELECT MAX(cnt)
  FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM conflicts_of_interest
    GROUP BY paper_id
  )
)
ORDER BY p.paper_id
gold_sql:
WITH paper_conflict_counts AS (
  SELECT
    p.paper_id,
    p.title,
    COUNT(coi.conflict_id) AS conflict_count
  FROM papers AS p
  LEFT JOIN conflicts_of_interest AS coi
    ON coi.paper_id = p.paper_id
  GROUP BY p.paper_id, p.title
),
max_conflict_paper AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(conflict_count) AS max_conflict_count
  FROM paper_conflict_counts
)
SELECT
  pcc.paper_id,
  pcc.title,
  pcc.conflict_count AS max_conflict_count
FROM paper_conflict_counts AS pcc
JOIN max_conflict_paper AS mcp
  ON pcc.conflict_count = mcp.max_conflict_count
ORDER BY pcc.paper_id
question: Which paper has the greatest number of declared conflicts of interest, and what is its paper ID, title, and total conflict count? If more than one paper shares the same highest conflict count, report every such paper and sort the results by paper ID.

gate.row_grain: a paper that shares the maximum count of declared conflicts of interest
columns: total count of declared conflicts of interest
gate.why: The result set size is variable because multiple papers may tie for the maximum number of conflicts of interest.

WITH project_dates AS (
  SELECT
    fp.project_id,
    fp.application_id,
    MIN(fp.funding_start_date) AS funding_start_date,
    MAX(fp.funding_end_date) AS funding_end_date
  FROM funded_projects AS fp
  GROUP BY fp.project_id, fp.application_id
),
publication_counts AS (
  SELECT
    project_id,
    COUNT(*) AS publication_count
  FROM publications
  GROUP BY project_id
)
SELECT
  a.application_id AS application_id,
  pd.project_id AS project_id,
  pd.funding_start_date AS funding_start_date,
  pd.funding_end_date AS funding_end_date,
  julianday(pd.funding_end_date) - julianday(pd.funding_start_date) AS funding_span_days,
  COALESCE(pc.publication_count, 0) AS publication_count
FROM applications AS a
JOIN project_dates AS pd
  ON a.application_id = pd.application_id
LEFT JOIN publication_counts AS pc
  ON pd.project_id = pc.project_id
ORDER BY funding_span_days DESC, a.application_id
question: For each funded project, report the application ID, project ID, earliest funding start date, latest funding end date, the funding span in days between those two dates, and the number of publications produced by that project. Order the projects from the longest funding span to the shortest, breaking ties by application ID.

gate.why: The question clearly specifies the metrics to compute for each funded project, the exact columns required, and the sorting order.

WITH edu_stats AS (
  SELECT
    i.education_id,
    e.education_name,
    e.education_num,
    COUNT(*) AS total_individuals,
    SUM(CASE WHEN i.immigrant_status = (SELECT immigrant_status_id FROM immigrant_statuses WHERE immigrant_status_name = 'Yes' LIMIT 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS immigrant_count
  FROM individuals AS i
  JOIN educations AS e
    ON i.education_id = e.education_id
  GROUP BY i.education_id, e.education_name, e.education_num
),
ranked_edu AS (
  SELECT
    education_name,
    education_num,
    total_individuals,
    immigrant_count,
    ROUND(1.0 * immigrant_count / total_individuals, 3) AS immigrant_rate,
    CASE
      WHEN 1.0 * immigrant_count / total_individuals >= 0.5 THEN 'high'
      WHEN 1.0 * immigrant_count / total_individuals >= 0.2 THEN 'medium'
      ELSE 'low'
    END AS immigrant_rate_label
  FROM edu_stats
)
SELECT
  education_name,
  education_num,
  total_individuals AS denominator_count,
  immigrant_count AS numerator_count,
  immigrant_rate,
  immigrant_rate_label
FROM ranked_edu
ORDER BY immigrant_rate DESC, total_individuals DESC

gold_sql:
WITH qualified_flights AS (
  SELECT f.flight_id
  FROM flights f
  JOIN data_quality dq
    ON dq.flight_id = f.flight_id
  JOIN environmental_conditions ec
    ON ec.flight_id = f.flight_id
  WHERE dq.metric_name = 'accuracy'
    AND dq.metric_value >= 0.9
    AND ec.windspeed_kts < 20
  GROUP BY f.flight_id
  HAVING AVG(dq.metric_value) >= 0.9
),
ordered_quality AS (
  SELECT
    dq.flight_id,
    SUM(dq.metric_value) AS flight_quality_total
  FROM data_quality dq
  JOIN qualified_flights qf
    ON qf.flight_id = dq.flight_id
  GROUP BY dq.flight_id
)
SELECT
  flight_id,
  flight_quality_total,
  SUM(flight_quality_total) OVER (ORDER BY flight_quality_total, flight_id) AS running_quality_total
FROM ordered_quality
ORDER BY flight_quality_total, flight_id

WITH crop_set AS (
  SELECT c.crop_id,
         c.crop_name,
         SUM(mp.price) AS total_price,
         COUNT(mp.price_id) AS price_points
  FROM crops c
  JOIN market_prices mp
    ON c.crop_id = mp.crop_id
  WHERE c.crop_type = 'grain'
  GROUP BY c.crop_id, c.crop_name
),
ranked_crops AS (
  SELECT crop_id,
         crop_name,
         total_price,
         price_points,
         SUM(total_price) OVER (ORDER BY total_price DESC) AS cumulative_price_total
  FROM crop_set
)
SELECT MAX(cumulative_price_total) AS max_cumulative_price_total
FROM ranked_crops
question: For all crops classified as grains, calculate the total market price summed across all recorded price entries for each crop, and also count how many price records each crop has. Then, order those grain crops by their total market price from highest to lowest, compute the running cumulative sum of those total market prices in that order, and report the single largest cumulative value reached.

WITH soil_stats AS (
  SELECT
    r.soil_id,
    COUNT(*) AS result_count,
    AVG(r.p_soil_meanARID) AS avg_soil_arid,
    MAX(r.precipitation_yearTotal) AS max_precipitation,
    AVG(r.p_water) AS avg_water_content,
    COUNT(r.simulation_id) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) AS simulation_id_ratio
  FROM results r
  WHERE r.soil_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY r.soil_id
)
SELECT
  s.soil_id,
  s.soil_name,
  ss.result_count,
  ss.simulation_id_ratio,
  ss.avg_soil_arid,
  ss.max_precipitation,
  CASE
    WHEN ss.avg_soil_arid < 300 THEN 'low_arid'
    WHEN ss.avg_soil_arid < 700 THEN 'moderate_arid'
    ELSE 'high_arid'
  END AS arid_label
FROM soil_stats ss
JOIN soils s
  ON s.soil_id = ss.soil_id
ORDER BY ss.result_count DESC, s.soil_name
question: For each soil, please provide the soil ID, soil name, number of result records, the share of result records that have a simulation ID, the average soil ARID, the maximum yearly precipitation, and an aridity label based on the average soil ARID. Use “low_arid” when the average is below 300, “moderate_arid” when it is at least 300 but below 700, and “high_arid” otherwise. Order the soils from most result records to fewest, and then by soil name.

columns: share of result records with a simulation ID
gate.why: The prompt clearly defines the requested fields, calculations, conditional categorization logic, and ordering for each soil.

measure: a label assigned by thresholds on a computed quantity
naive_sql:
SELECT
  ai.index_name AS index_name,
  COUNT(al.alert_log_id) AS alert_log_count,
  COUNT(asg.alert_id) AS alert_setting_count,
  ROUND(AVG(asg.threshold_value), 2) AS avg_threshold_value,
  CASE
    WHEN AVG(asg.threshold_value) >= 200 THEN 'high'
    WHEN AVG(asg.threshold_value) >= 100 THEN 'medium'
    ELSE 'low'
  END AS threshold_label
FROM air_quality_indexes AS ai
JOIN alert_settings AS asg
  ON asg.index_id = ai.index_id
JOIN alert_logs AS al
  ON al.alert_id = asg.alert_id
GROUP BY ai.index_id, ai.index_name
ORDER BY ai.index_name
gold_sql:
WITH alert_counts AS (
  SELECT
    asg.index_id AS index_id,
    COUNT(al.alert_log_id) AS alert_log_count
  FROM alert_settings AS asg
  LEFT JOIN alert_logs AS al
    ON al.alert_id = asg.alert_id
  GROUP BY asg.index_id
),
index_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    ai.index_id AS index_id,
    ai.index_name AS index_name,
    COALESCE(ac.alert_log_count, 0) AS alert_log_count,
    COUNT(asg.alert_id) AS alert_setting_count,
    ROUND(AVG(asg.threshold_value), 2) AS avg_threshold_value
  FROM air_quality_indexes AS ai
  LEFT JOIN alert_settings AS asg
    ON asg.index_id = ai.index_id
  LEFT JOIN alert_counts AS ac
    ON ac.index_id = ai.index_id
  GROUP BY ai.index_id, ai.index_name, ac.alert_log_count
)
SELECT
  index_name,
  alert_log_count,
  alert_setting_count,
  avg_threshold_value,
  CASE
    WHEN avg_threshold_value >= 200 THEN 'high'
    WHEN avg_threshold_value >= 100 THEN 'medium'
    ELSE 'low'
  END AS threshold_label
FROM index_metrics
ORDER BY index_name
